title: Multiple Germline Events Contribute to Cancer Development in Patients with Li-Fraumeni Syndrome.
authors: Subasri, Vallijah; Light, Nicholas; Kanwar, Nisha; Brzezinski, Jack; Luo, Ping; Hansford, Jordan R; Cairney, Elizabeth; Portwine, Carol; Elser, Christine; Finlay, Jonathan L; Nichols, Kim E; Alon, Noa; Brunga, Ledia; Anson, Jo; Kohlmann, Wendy; de Andrade, Kelvin C; Khincha, Payal P; Savage, Sharon A; Schiffman, Joshua D; Weksberg, Rosanna; Pugh, Trevor J; Villani, Anita; Shlien, Adam; Goldenberg, Anna; Malkin, David
one_liner_zh: 该研究利用全基因组测序和甲基化分析探讨Li-Fraumeni综合征的癌症易感性，虽含机器学习预测模型，但核心是遗传/表观遗传变异与癌症风险，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模。
abstract: Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS) is an autosomal dominant cancer-predisposition disorder. Approximately 70% of individuals who fit the clinical definition of LFS harbor a pathogenic germline variant in the TP53 tumor suppressor gene. However, the remaining 30% of patients lack a TP53 variant and even among variant TP53 carriers, approximately 20% remain cancer-free. Understanding the variable cancer penetrance and phenotypic variability in LFS is critical to developing rational approaches to accurate, early tumor detection and risk-reduction strategies. We leveraged family-based whole-genome sequencing and DNA methylation to evaluate the germline genomes of a large, multi-institutional cohort of patients with LFS (n = 396) with variant (n = 374) or wildtype TP53 (n = 22). We identified alternative cancer-associated genetic aberrations in 8/14 wildtype TP53 carriers who developed cancer. Among variant TP53 carriers, 19/49 who developed cancer harbored a pathogenic variant in another cancer gene. Modifier variants in the WNT signaling pathway were associated with decreased cancer incidence. Furthermore, we leveraged the noncoding genome and methylome to identify inherited epimutations in genes including ASXL1, ETV6, and LEF1 that confer increased cancer risk. Using these epimutations, we built a machine learning model that can predict cancer risk in patients with LFS with an area under the receiver operator characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.725 (0.633-0.810). SIGNIFICANCE: Our study clarifies the genomic basis for the phenotypic variability in LFS and highlights the immense benefits of expanding genetic and epigenetic testing of patients with LFS beyond TP53. More broadly, it necessitates the dissociation of hereditary cancer syndromes as single gene disorders and emphasizes the importance of understanding these diseases in a holistic manner as opposed to through the lens of a single gene.
abstract_zh: Li-Fraumeni综合征（LFS）是一种常染色体显性遗传的癌症易感性疾病。符合LFS临床定义的个体中，约70%携带TP53肿瘤抑制基因的致病性胚系变异。然而，其余30%的患者缺乏TP53变异，即使在TP53变异携带者中，约20%仍保持无癌状态。理解LFS中癌症外显率的变异性和表型多样性，对于制定合理策略以实现准确、早期肿瘤检测和风险降低措施至关重要。我们利用基于家系的全基因组测序和DNA甲基化分析，评估了一个大型多机构LFS患者队列（n = 396）的胚系基因组，其中包含TP53变异携带者（n = 374）或野生型TP53携带者（n = 22）。我们在8/14名发展为癌症的野生型TP53携带者中识别出替代性癌症相关遗传畸变。在TP53变异携带者中，19/49名发展为癌症的患者携带另一个癌症基因的致病性变异。WNT信号通路中的修饰性变异与癌症发病率降低相关。此外，我们利用非编码基因组和甲基化组，识别出包括ASXL1、ETV6和LEF1在内的基因中的遗传性表观突变，这些突变赋予增加的癌症风险。利用这些表观突变，我们构建了一个机器学习模型，可预测LFS患者的癌症风险，其受试者工作特征曲线下面积（AUROC）为0.725（0.633-0.810）。意义：我们的研究阐明了LFS表型多样性的基因组基础，并强调了将LFS患者的遗传和表观遗传检测扩展到TP53之外的巨大益处。更广泛地，这要求将遗传性癌症综合征视为非单基因疾病，并强调以整体方式而非单一基因视角理解这些疾病的重要性。
